idea: Replace the random-order baseline with a filter-then-fill curator. (1) Build a target-domain classifier: fit a TfidfVectorizer (word 1-2grams, sublinear_tf, max_features ~200k, lowercase=False, token_pattern keeping punctuation tokens like '@-@' and '=') on the first ~3000 chars of every pool doc plus the 200 target_sample docs; compute each pool doc's cosine similarity to the centroid of the target_sample vectors. Also compute cheap structural features per doc: starts with '= Title =' header line, fraction of non-ASCII chars, fraction of spam keywords ('discount code', 'coupon', 'free shipping', 'cheap', 'buy now', 'Click here'). (2) Detect word-shuffled damaged docs (WikiText-looking but scrambled word order): build a bigram set/counter from target_sample (plus the top-similarity pool docs), and for each doc score the fraction of its adjacent word bigrams (on first ~400 words after the title line) that appear in that reference bigram set; also use simple signals such as the rate of sentences/lines beginning with ' ,' or '. ' followed by lowercase and the fraction of ' . ' tokens followed by a lowercase word. Drop docs whose bigram-hit rate falls in the low mode (choose threshold with a 2-cluster split / Otsu on the scores of WikiText-header docs). (3) Deduplicate: drop exact duplicates by hash of normalized text and near-duplicates by hash of the first 500 chars. (4) Keep docs that pass: WikiText-like (header or centroid similarity above an Otsu threshold), not shuffled, not spam, non-ASCII fraction low, not duplicate. (5) Order kept docs in a seeded random shuffle (CURATE_SEED) and return that list; if kept tokens < T (count with tiktoken gpt2 or estimate len/4), let it cycle naturally rather than padding with junk. Print counts of each bucket for diagnostics.
why: The pool sample shows roughly half the tokens are spam, off-domain web text, homoglyph-corrupted text and word-shuffled WikiText articles, so training only on clean, deduplicated, in-order WikiText-style articles (cycled if needed) should give the largest first-step bpb drop over the unfiltered baseline.

idea:

For each doc that has a '= Title =' first line and is not spam or junk, set toks = doc.split() (full doc) and cut it into consecutive 300-token windows, dropping a last window under 150 tokens (a doc under 300 tokens is one window). For each window compute the same function-bigram rate as now (same 15 pairs, hits / window length). Compute m as the median of the full-document rate over target_sample. A window is bad if its rate < 0.3 * m. Mark the doc shuffled (tier C) if its first-500-token rate < 0.3 * m (the current rule) OR more than 25% of its windows are bad.

2. Vocabulary check for character-level damage. Build vocab as the set of whitespace tokens that occur in target_sample (full text), plus tokens that occur in at least 5 different header docs of the pool (count document frequency on the first 2000 tokens of each header doc). For each candidate tier A doc compute oov = fraction of its first 2000 tokens not in vocab. Let med and mad be the median and the median absolute deviation of oov over the candidate A docs. Demote a doc to tier C if oov > med + 6 * mad and oov > 0.25.

3. Near-duplicate check inside tier A only. Key = (first line, ' '.join(toks[20:60])). Keep the first doc for each key and send the others to tier D.
